content.text: cath ablation = preferred; if ablation isn’t an option: oral verapamil or diltiazem = recommended; oral digoxin or amiodarone may be reasonable.
individualized by age, lean body wt, renal funct and other drugs; if loading, give ½ the total load first, then ¼ every 6–8 h twice; lower maintenance doses in renal impairment.

digoxin = a P-gp substrate, so P-gp inhibitors/inducers Δ its levels; amiodarone raises digoxin levels: halve the digoxin dose (or stop it) and watch for toxicity; check a level b4 starting an interacting drug.
<0.5 ng/mL loses efficacy and >2 ng/mL adds toxicity w.o benefit; draw just b4 the next dose or ≥6 h after the last dose, and don't Δ the dose on one isolated level.

N/V, visual chgs and arrhythmias; ↔ VT, nonparoxysmal junctional tachy in AF and hyperkalemia are serious signs; hypokalemia or hypomagnesemia allows toxicity @ lower levels. Stop digoxin, monitor, keep K 4.0–5.5; Digoxin Immune Fab for life-threatening arrhythmias or hyperkalemia; atropine for brady/♡ block; ⍉removed by dialysis.
report N/V, persistent diarrhea, confusion, weakness or visual chgs (blurred or green-yellow vision, halos), which can mean the dose = too ↑.
